The Argentine pope succeeded Pope Benedi.why: 'The Argentine pope' is a common description of Francis, and his succeeding Benedict XVI is a common fact, but the two are not joined. Common sense: people say Francis was the Argentine pope and that he succeeded Benedict XVI; nobody says it as 'the Argentine pope succeeded Benedict', because the name already carries both, so it is true but not said on its own.

The pope whom Pope Francis succeeded was.why: His birthplace is written of Benedict XVI by name, and almost never through the description 'the pope Francis succeeded'; the description has to be resolved first. Common sense: people say Benedict XVI was born in Marktl and that he came before Francis; nobody gives the birth town of 'the pope before Francis', so it is true but not said on its own. The exact joined forms were counted and are rare (counts in the sources).
